title: TTB: Processing Times for Label Applications (COLA)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (ttb.gov)
source_type: Government web page with live agency statistics
reliability: Government document; TTB is also the agency that imposes and administers the label approval requirement. Median figures are the agency's own reporting and the page is a live snapshot.
findings: Page states it was updated 11/4/2026 7:00 AM and shows median label processing times of 6 days for distilled spirits labels, 1 day for malt beverage labels and 2 days for wine labels, with TTB working on applications received 10/30/2026, 11/03/2026 and 11/02/2026 respectively.
TTB states its customer service goal is to complete review of 85% of label applications within 15 days, and reports 139,048 label applications received in 2026 to date.

TTB defines label processing time as the median days from receipt until approval or rejection, including time spent sending electronic applications back and forth for correction; applications resubmitted for correction take priority over new applications.
TTB states there is no fee to apply through COLAs Online.
limitations: Live page: figures change daily and this record is a single snapshot on the access date; the page publication date is not stated.
Medians hide the tail: no distribution, rejection rate, or number of resubmission rounds was shown.
A median measured after approval or rejection does not capture label design, legal review or rework costs borne by the producer.
